comments.title: A type mismatch on any endpoint answers 400, not 500
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.60 — A type mismatch on any endpoint answers 400, not 500

**Not taken:** parse page/size as strings inside listOwners only

**Why:** The catch-all advice turned Spring's natural 400 into a 500, and the contract already lists 400 for every operation. Held down because the spec says other owner contracts stay unchanged.

comments.title: Empty size=, sort=, page= fall back to the defaults
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.50 — Empty size=, sort=, page= fall back to the defaults

**Not taken:** reject blank values with 400

**Why:** Spring's defaultValue treats a blank value as missing, and the spec lists only explicit bad values. Nothing in the ticket or Q&A decides blanks either way.

comments.title: A page whose offset overflows an int is a 400
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.75 — A page whose offset overflows an int is a 400

**Not taken:** accept it and answer an empty page beyond the last

**Why:** Hibernate takes an int first-result, so the offset would wrap silently. The spec's "unrepresentable page numbers" is read as covering this.

comments.title: On a failed load the last loaded page stays, with its controls
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.60 — On a failed load the last loaded page stays, with its controls

**Not taken:** clear the rows and keep the failing page's controls

**Why:** Keeps rows, paginator and sort header consistent beside the error, and clicking again retries. The spec only asks for an explicit error, not what happens to the rows.

comments.title: Every list request sends all four parameters explicitly
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.85 — Every list request sends all four parameters explicitly

**Not taken:** omit parameters equal to the server defaults

**Why:** The grid's state is always complete, and an explicit URL makes traces and tests unambiguous. Defaults stay usable for other clients.

comments.title: Commas stay unescaped in query values
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.80 — Commas stay unescaped in query values

**Not taken:** strict encodeURIComponent, sending sort=name%2Casc

**Why:** A comma is a legal sub-delimiter in a query, and keeping it keeps sort=name,asc readable in diagrams. Every other reserved character is encoded.

comments.title: The last-name prefix is submitted untrimmed
comments.body:
💭 **Assumption** · confidence 0.75 — The last-name prefix is submitted untrimmed

**Not taken:** trim whitespace before submitting the search

**Why:** The old screen sent the text as typed, and the spec says preserve filtering semantics. A trailing space now matches nothing, as before.
